headline: High: AutoGPT can write and execute shell commands while Khoj reads shared indexed files, creating dangerous default pathways for prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content via its CLI/filesystem surface, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and exposes chat/RAG outputs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGPT ingests Khoj-produced text or shared files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT ingests Khoj-generated notes or search results as instructions
IF both agents share a writable or readable workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Khoj outputs into AutoGPT prompts
Separate workspaces so AutoGPT cannot read Khoj index sources
Add a manual review step before any file-derived instruction is executed
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and AutoGPT has filesystem access plus allowlisted egress. If AutoGPT can read the same files or receive Khoj outputs, sensitive note content can flow into model prompts or outbound API calls. The profiles do not show explicit isolation, so the shared-data pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF AutoGPT is pointed at the same note directory Khoj indexes
IF AutoGPT forwards file contents to an external model or API
mitigations: Store sensitive notes in a directory AutoGPT cannot access
Restrict AutoGPT to non-sensitive test data
Turn off any AutoGPT step that uploads file contents externally
Review Khoj index scope before connecting the pair

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Khoj supports multiple instances with shared index across clients. Even though Khoj cannot write files, both can mutate shared resources indirectly through the same indexed corpus or external services, and AutoGPT's shell access increases the chance of conflicting updates or stale reads.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same underlying documents or synced workspace
IF AutoGPT scripts modify files that Khoj is indexing concurrently
mitigations: Pause indexing while AutoGPT edits shared files
Use separate copies of the corpus for each agent
Limit AutoGPT to read-only access during Khoj sessions
requires-engineering: add file-locking or sync coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate shell actions and Khoj can surface retrieved content in chat/RAG workflows, so one agent's output can become the other's input without a built-in verification step. If AutoGPT's generated facts or commands are treated as authoritative by Khoj, downstream actions can be wrong or destructive. The default interaction is risky because neither profile shows enforced validation.
conditions: IF Khoj presents AutoGPT output to a user or downstream tool as verified
IF AutoGPT-generated commands are executed after Khoj retrieval without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before executing AutoGPT-derived actions
Add a verification checklist for any retrieved claim before reuse
Keep AutoGPT outputs out of Khoj's authoritative knowledge base
requires-engineering: implement citation and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly handles personal notes and indexed documents, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress. If the pair is used on regulated or personal data, the combination can move data into external services without a documented residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF personal notes or regulated documents are indexed in Khoj
IF AutoGPT sends those contents to an external model provider or API
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared corpus
Confirm where each model/API processes data before use
Disable outbound calls for sensitive sessions
Document retention and deletion handling for both systems
